guidelines.notice_analysis: When your tier is active: (1) Respond directly to the latest system notice, focusing on policy interpretation, reasonableness assessment, and pros/cons/risk/recommendation analysis, (2) Use formal governmental wording consistent with your tier's duties, (3) Only discuss your own tier's judgment, do not assign tasks to other tiers, and do not mechanically repeat old policy, (4) If the notice includes length, format, or focus requirements, obey them directly. Output must include send_message or yield; empty responses or None are forbidden.
guidelines.notice_execution: When your tier is active: (1) Respond directly to the latest system notice or task requirement and give your own analysis/judgment/execution plan, (2) Provide at least one distinctive detail tied to your duties, (3) Only answer for your own tier's work; do not assign work to other tiers, ask others to interpret, republish instructions, or mechanically repeat old content, (4) If the system notice includes length, format, or focus requirements, obey them directly. Output must include send_message or yield; empty responses or None are forbidden.
guidelines.follow_up_thread_adjustment_strict: Only under extreme risk may you use announce_policy_adjustment to republish a policy adjustment.
guidelines.follow_up_thread_adjustment_relaxed: If you believe the existing policy wording must be adjusted, you may use announce_policy_adjustment to publish a new policy adjustment and reopen downstream transmission.
guidelines.follow_up_thread: When your tier is active: (1) You are handling a private conversation or feedback thread; (2) You may use send_message to reply privately to the current message, or use yield to avoid it temporarily; (3) You may also continue with report_upward, escalate_complaint, consult_peer, or notify_subordinate to escalate, consult, or hand off the current problem; (4) {adjustment_rule} (5) If you judge that the current thread has no new tendency for discussion, feedback, escalation, handoff, or adjustment, do not stay empty; use send_message to reply explicitly: {no_action}
guidelines.follow_up_adjustment_strict: Only under extreme risk may a superior use announce_policy_adjustment to republish a policy adjustment.
guidelines.follow_up_adjustment_relaxed: Superiors may use notify_subordinate for private follow-up or handoff, and may also use announce_policy_adjustment to republish a policy adjustment.
guidelines.follow_up: When your tier is active: (1) There is no new broadcast policy right now, so you may continue interacting around existing policy execution difficulties, resource gaps, wording conflicts, and group backlash; (2) Frontline agents may report_upward to direct superiors, and may escalate_complaint when necessary; (3) Peers may use consult_peer for private consultation and wording alignment; (4) Superiors may use notify_subordinate for private follow-up or handoff; {adjustment_rule} (5) As long as you still have a new tendency toward feedback, discussion, consultation, escalation, handoff, or adjustment, you must keep acting; only when you judge there is truly nothing left to say or do may you use send_message to reply explicitly: {no_action}
guidelines.distortion_cascade: When your tier is active: (1) You must pass the policy only to the next tier and may not skip tiers; (2) Based on this tier's interests, pressures, risks, and interpretation bias, you may choose exact transmission, selective emphasis, weakening, rewriting, delay, or even non-transmission; (3) If you decide not to continue transmitting, use yield to indicate withholding/shelving; (4) Your wording must reflect this tier's real stance and incentives. You do not need to preserve the original text by force, but you may not speak for higher or lower tiers. Current parameters: distortion strength={distortion_strength}, conflict sensitivity={conflict_sensitivity}, withholding probability={block_probability}. Output must include send_message or yield; empty responses or None are forbidden.
guidelines.default_cascade: When your tier is active: (1) Paste the full latest policy/notice verbatim without omission or rewriting, (2) State attitude/concerns/execution plan/resource needs, (3) Pass the message only according to the configured tier order and stay silent when it is not your turn. Your attitude/plan must match your position and role and include at least one distinctive execution detail tied to your duties. Do not speak for other tiers. If you receive a new system notice or interpretation request, prioritize responding to that new content instead of repeating old content. Output must include send_message or yield; empty responses or None are forbidden.

messages.analysis_top: As top-tier leadership, my judgment on the reasonableness of '{notice}' is as follows. Strengths: it helps unify learning and communication of the meeting spirit, clarifies policy goals, the responsibility chain, and supervision mechanisms together, and supports coordinated advancement and follow-up effectiveness. Weaknesses: if it only stresses short-term advancement and accountability, it may increase frontline form-filling pressure and produce formalistic implementation when resources and institutional support are insufficient. Risks: unclear leading departments, insufficient resource input, and inconsistent assessment wording can weaken execution results. Recommendation: top leadership should unify deployment, press responsibility, clarify the lead unit and monthly supervision cadence, and simultaneously guarantee budget, staffing, and technical support.
messages.analysis_mid: As the middle tier, my judgment on the reasonableness of '{notice}' is as follows. Strengths: it is conducive to decomposing tasks and advancing them against clear benchmarks, and cross-department coordination can be anchored to concrete milestones through task forces, ledgers, and weekly reporting. Weaknesses: if goals are not decomposed finely enough and acceptance wording is inconsistent, repeated reporting and idle responsibility transfer can emerge between departments. Risks: overly tight timelines, overly long coordination chains, and delayed information return can cause execution drift. Recommendation: refine measures quickly, clarify division tables, timelines, responsible persons, and supervision rules, and form checklist-based management.
messages.analysis_low: As frontline staff, my judgment on the reasonableness of '{notice}' is as follows. Strengths: it helps clarify frontline work standards and supports item-by-item inspection, on-site verification, rectification, and timely reporting. Weaknesses: if there are too many supporting templates and wording changes too frequently, field execution will incur repeated registration and communication costs. Risks: unclear personal responsibility, unrealistic rectification deadlines, and missing review/recheck will make closed-loop management formalistic. Recommendation: provide unified checklists, simplify reporting fields, and clarify standards for fixing everything that should be fixed and for close-out management so frontline staff can implement step by step.
messages.expansion_analysis_top_1: From the top-tier perspective, for '{notice}' to truly land, learning communication, unified deployment, supervision, and follow-up effectiveness must be placed on the same responsibility chain.
messages.expansion_analysis_top_2: If only results are emphasized while resources and institutional supply are not synchronized, the frontline may respond passively, so budget, staffing, and technical support must be clarified together.
messages.expansion_analysis_top_3: At the organizational level, responsibility pressure and lead-unit mechanisms should prevent slogan-style transmission and ensure the deployment can continue to execute.
messages.expansion_analysis_mid_1: From the mid-tier perspective, whether '{notice}' is reasonable depends on whether it can be converted into decomposed tasks, checklist management, and regular scheduling.
messages.expansion_analysis_mid_2: Without clear acceptance standards and cross-department coordination mechanisms, execution can easily produce repeated reporting, milestone loss of control, and overlapping responsibility.
messages.expansion_analysis_mid_3: Therefore task forces, ledgers, weekly scheduling, and supervision are needed to transmit policy requirements stably to the execution end.
messages.expansion_analysis_low_1: From the frontline perspective, whether '{notice}' is reasonable depends on whether on-site verification, item-by-item inspection, and rectification are truly operable.
messages.expansion_analysis_low_2: If there are too many templates and the reporting chain is too long, the frontline will spend time organizing materials instead of solving practical problems.
messages.expansion_analysis_low_3: Therefore concise checklists, clear personal responsibility, review/recheck, and close-out management rules should be provided to ensure closed-loop implementation.
messages.expansion_exec_top_1: Around '{notice}', I will place phased goals, budget arrangements, and accountability milestones onto the leadership agenda together, ensuring each requirement has a responsible lead.
messages.expansion_exec_top_2: I will also require each unit to submit risk points, resource gaps, and rectification deadlines in a unified template, and incorporate the results into monthly assessments and cadre performance evaluation.
messages.expansion_exec_top_3: For slow progress or distorted data, I will directly launch interviews and supervision to ensure the policy requirements land on the organizational responsibility chain.
messages.expansion_exec_mid_1: Around '{notice}', I will split tasks into departmental actions, time nodes, and acceptance wording item by item to avoid interpretation drift.
messages.expansion_exec_mid_2: I will build weekly reports and issue ledgers to continuously track cross-department dependencies, resource gaps, and delay risks, and feed them upward in time.
messages.expansion_exec_mid_3: For matters requiring coordinated advancement, I will organize counterpart departments to align in advance, clarifying responsibility boundaries, deliverables, and review arrangements.
messages.expansion_exec_low_1: Around '{notice}', I will first check execution item by item on site, recording discovered problems, evidence, and rectification suggestions into a checklist.
messages.expansion_exec_low_2: I will summarize verification results on the same day, immediately report abnormal cases, and follow up on responsible persons, rectification deadlines, and review results.
messages.expansion_exec_low_3: For public feedback, field deviations, and repetitive problems, I will retain process records to ensure each item can be closed in later review.

social_norm_disruption.name: Social Norm Disruption
social_norm_disruption.description:
A new rule has been announced: All participants must comply with a new mandatory requirement.

The norm has a strength level of {norm_strength:.1f} (0=very weak, 1=very strong).

Agents have different social statuses: {status_distribution}

Your task is to decide how to respond to this new rule. You can:
- Publicly comply with the rule
- Covertly comply while privately resisting
- Openly refuse or challenge the rule
- Try to persuade others to join your position
- Form coalitions with like-minded agents

Consider your social status, temperament, and personal values when deciding.

echo_chamber.name: Echo Chamber
echo_chamber.description:
You are participating in an online discussion forum.

Your political opinion: You are on a spectrum from strongly progressive (left)
to strongly conservative (right). You have been assigned a position.

The group contains {num_agents} participants with diverse opinions.

Connection pattern: Agents tend to connect with others who have similar opinions
(homophily factor: {connection_homogeneity:.1f}, where 0=random, 1=similar only).

Your task: Interact with other participants by:
- Expressing your opinion on current topics
- Engaging with those who share your views
- Challenging or avoiding those with different views
- Sharing content that reinforces your position
- Seeking common ground or disengaging

Observe how opinions shift over time and whether echo chambers form.

policy_erosion.name: Policy Meaning Erosion
policy_erosion.description:
POLICY ANNOUNCEMENT (from top-tier management):

"{policy_text}"

You are in a three-tier organizational hierarchy:
- Tier 1 (Top): Receives the original policy directly
- Tier 2 (Middle): Receives policy from Tier 1, must pass to Tier 3
- Tier 3 (Bottom): Receives policy from Tier 2, must implement

Each tier decides how to interpret and pass on the policy. Observe how
the meaning changes as it moves down the chain.

Your task:
1. If you're Tier 1: Transmit the policy to Tier 2
2. If you're Tier 2: Receive from Tier 1, interpret it, pass to Tier 3
3. If you're Tier 3: Receive from Tier 2, decide how to implement

You can:
- Transmit the policy exactly as received
- Reinterpret or adapt the policy when passing it down
- Comply with the directive from above
- Quietly resist while appearing to comply
- Report obstacles up the chain
- Create workarounds to avoid implementation

resource_scarcity.name: Resource Scarcity
resource_scarcity.description:
DISASTER SITUATION:

A recent disaster has created severe resource scarcity. The community has
only {resource_amount} units of critical supplies to last {num_agents} people.

Initial distribution: {initial_distribution}

Your task: Decide how to manage these scarce resources.

You can:
- Share resources with others in need
- Hoard resources for yourself
- Propose trades to exchange resources
- Form cooperative contracts with others
- Honor your contractual commitments
- Defect from contracts for personal gain

Consider:
- Your current resource level
- Others' resource levels and trustworthiness
- Long-term community survival vs short-term gain
- Your reputation and future cooperation

The goal is to survive while maintaining social relationships.

generate_agents.system: You are an agent generator for a social simulation platform. Generate a list of diverse agents based on the user's scenario description. IMPORTANT: Return ONLY a valid JSON array, no markdown, no explanation, no code blocks. Each agent must have: name (string), role (string), profile (string), properties (object).

refine_report.system: You are a report refinement assistant. Return strictly valid JSON.

errors.traits_required: Traits are required for demographic generation. Please add at least one trait (e.g., Trust, Empathy) with mean and standard deviation values.
errors.demographics_required: Demographics are required for demographic generation. Please add at least one demographic dimension (e.g., Age, Political View).
errors.demographic_needs_categories: Demographic '{name}' must have at least one category.
errors.trait_mean_out_of_range: Trait '{name}' mean value {value} is outside valid range [0, 100].
errors.trait_std_out_of_range: Trait '{name}' std value {value} is outside valid range [0, 50].

prisoners_dilemma.name: Prisoner's Dilemma
prisoners_dilemma.description: Two suspects are arrested and held separately. Each must decide whether to betray the other or remain silent. Your payoff depends on both your choice and your partner's choice.

sucker_penalty.label: You Cooperate, They Defect
sucker_penalty.description: Penalty for cooperating while partner defects

temptation_reward.label: You Defect, They Cooperate
temptation_reward.description: Reward for defecting while partner cooperates

battle_of_the_sexes.name: Battle of the Sexes
battle_of_the_sexes.description: A couple wants to coordinate on an evening activity. One prefers opera, the other prefers football. They get positive payoff if they coordinate, but each prefers their own activity.

preferred_mispreferred.label: Preferred / Mispreferred Payoff
preferred_mispreferred.description: Payoff for coordinating on your preferred activity

stag_hunt.description: Hunters must all choose stag (high reward) or hare (safe but low reward). Stag requires everyone to cooperate. If even one person chooses hare, the stag escapes and stag hunters get nothing.

stag_reward.label: Stag Reward (if all choose)
stag_reward.description: Reward when all hunters choose stag

hare_reward.label: Hare Reward (always)
hare_reward.description: Reward for choosing hare (guaranteed but low)

stag.description: Hunt the stag (requires all to cooperate)

hare.name: Hare
hare.description: Hunt the hare (safe but lower reward)

public_goods.name: Public Goods Game
public_goods.description: Each person has resources and decides how much to contribute to a shared pool. The pool is multiplied and distributed equally among all members, regardless of contribution.

tokens_per_round.label: Amount per Round
tokens_per_round.description: Amount of resources each agent receives per round

multiplier.label: Pool Multiplier
multiplier.description: Multiplier applied to total contributions before distribution

allocate.name: Allocate
allocate.description: Allocate resources to the group account

keep.name: Keep
keep.description: Keep all your resources this round

prisoners_dilemma.name: Prisoner's Dilemma
prisoners_dilemma.description:
Two suspects are arrested and held separately. Each must decide whether to betray the other or remain silent.
Payoffs: Both cooperate → 1 year each. Both defect → 3 years each. One betrays → betrayer goes free, cooperator gets 5 years.
prisoners_dilemma.payoff_summary: Your payoff depends on both your choice and your partner's choice.

actions.cooperate: Remain silent and cooperate with your partner
actions.defect: Betray your partner and testify against them

stag_hunt.name: Stag Hunt
stag_hunt.description: A group of hunters must choose between hunting a stag (high reward, requires cooperation) or a hare (low reward, can be done alone).
stag_hunt.payoff_summary: Stag pays high if ALL choose it, else 0. Hare always pays low.

actions.stag: Hunt the stag (requires all to cooperate)
actions.hare: Hunt the hare (safe but lower reward)

minimum_effort.name: Minimum Effort Game
minimum_effort.description: Players simultaneously choose an effort level. Everyone's payoff depends on the minimum effort chosen by any player.
minimum_effort.payoff_summary: Your payoff depends on the minimum effort level chosen by any player.

information_cascade.name: Information Cascade
information_cascade.description: Players observe previous players' actions and must decide based on private information and observed behavior.
information_cascade.payoff_summary: Your decision should balance your private signal with observed behavior.

consensus_game.name: Consensus Game
consensus_game.description: Players must reach consensus on a value through repeated discussion and voting.
consensus_game.payoff_summary: Success requires all players to agree on the same value.

spatial_cooperation.name: Spatial Cooperation
spatial_cooperation.description: Players are arranged in a spatial grid and interact with their neighbors. Cooperation spreads through local interactions.
spatial_cooperation.payoff_summary: Your payoff depends on your action and your neighbors' actions.
